title: Value put to the test
odia: କାଚ, କାଚ, ମଣି, ମଣି, କିଣା ବିକା ବେଳେ ଜଣା ଜଣି
literal_meaning: Glass is glass, a gem is a gem; buying and selling reveal which is which.
explanation: Resemblance and confident claims are not enough to establish value. The saying imagines a transaction as the moment when differences become consequential. It can be used when an attractive promise finally has to face a practical test.
usage_example: Two suppliers make equally impressive promises; a buyer asks to see their finished work before deciding. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The image comes from comparing valuable objects with lookalikes. It is a metaphor about testing claims, not a guarantee that markets always recognise quality.
